claims.explanation: Mocetinostat is a class I HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by the ZEB1/EMT axis: ZEB1-driven, mesenchymal-like tumors depend on class I HDAC activity to maintain stemness and drug resistance, so mocetinostat restores miR-203 and kills these lines, while lines with intact epithelial differentiation and low ZEB1 are protected. Consistently, the most sensitive lines are enriched for TP53, PIK3CA, BRAF, and chromatin-modifier mutations that accompany aggressive, dedifferentiated phenotypes, whereas the protected lines include several sarcomas, mesotheliomas, and renal carcinomas with fewer such features.

features.basis: ZEB1-driven EMT and stemness confer class I HDAC dependence; mocetinostat reverses ZEB1 function (PMID 25872941)
TP53 mutation is highly enriched in the most killed lines and marks aggressive, dedifferentiated tumors
PIK3CA mutation appears repeatedly among the most sensitive lines, consistent with PI3K-driven survival signaling
BRAF-mutant melanomas and other BRAF-mutant lines are enriched in the sensitive group
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, NCIH1648) are among the most killed
ARID1A loss occurs in several highly sensitive lines, suggesting SWI/SNF-dependent chromatin vulnerability
KMT2C mutation is enriched in the most sensitive lines, implicating chromatin dysregulation
KMT2D mutation appears in multiple sensitive lines, consistent with epigenetic dependency
SMARCA4 mutation is present in several highly sensitive lines, suggesting chromatin-remodeler vulnerability
PTEN mutation is more common in the least affected lines (786O, ZR751, KALS1), suggesting reduced dependence
NF1 mutation appears in several resistant lines, possibly reflecting RAS/MAPK-driven resistance
CDKN2A mutation is enriched in the least affected lines, suggesting cell-cycle-independent survival
